messages:
maria: FYI CI nightly shows a p99 regression on main after the kernel-selection/heuristics merge. Canary blocked. https://ci.internal/reports/1939900000 :confused:
ci-bot: nightly-run #19399 failed - p99 increased by 2.1x, affected tests: runtime/high_seq_throughput.test
kai: Ack. I glanced at the artifacts earlier — stack traces point to kernel_selector scoring path. Could be the new candidate-prioritization changes or batching window tweak.
jonah: Can someone bisect? If it's between the kernel selector refactor and batching tweak we should narrow it before reverting anything big.
maria: Starting a local repro now. Minimal run: `./tools/repro --test=high_seq --seq=2048 --profile`

maria: Repro log snippet:
```
2026-03-17T02:12:11.123Z INFO run: seq=2048 iterations=50
2026-03-17T02:15:04.456Z PERF p50=30ms p95=120ms p99=420ms
2026-03-17T02:15:04.457Z PROFILE top: kernel_selector::score_candidates (45%), scoring_cache::get (18%), batching::window_eval (12%)
```

rachel: Interesting that scoring_cache::get shows up. That cache was added recently, right?
kai: Yep — two suspect commits: `ab12ef3` batching open-window change, and `e7f9c2` scoring cache + candidate reordering.
jonah: Plan: git bisect between the last-known-good nightly and main, run the repro as the test command. I can kick off a bisect-runner on CI: `git bisect start -- bad=HEAD good=origin/nightly-good && git bisect run ./tools/bisect-run.sh --test high_seq`
rachel: I can run that on the bisect runner, but need to coordinate with CI usage. Anyone object?
maria: Go ahead. I also tried a manual quick-check: `git checkout e7f9c2~1 && bazel build //runtime && ./tools/repro --seq=2048` -> p99 back to ~180ms. So e7f9c2 looks suspicious.
ci-bot: bisect-runner started, estimate ~18 steps to locate commit. Logs: https://ci.internal/bisect/1939900000

rachel: After ~12 steps bisect narrowed to `e7f9c2` (author: derek) - commit message "kernel: add scoring cache and reorder heuristics".
maria: That matches my local repro. Profile shows lock contention in scoring_cache::get (mutex). Hot path mutex is bad for high-concurrency sequences.
kai: If it's a mutex, that's an easy explanation for p99 blowup. Score cache might have been intended to save work, but adding a central lock can regress.
jonah: Can we try a minimal revert for the scoring cache to confirm? `git revert e7f9c2 --no-edit && bazel build && ./tools/repro`
maria: I just tried a local revert. Results: p99 returned to normal. Confirmed.
rachel: I'm opening a rollback PR to unblock canary: #4561 (rollback e7f9c2). Marking rollout blocked in the canary dashboard.
deploy-bot: Rollback PR #4561 created by rachel and assigned to infra-oncall. Canary flagged as BLOCKED.
derek: @maria @rachel thanks for the heads up — my change introduced a scoring cache with a single global mutex to protect the LRU list. I see how that creates contention at high seq lengths. I'll push a fix that shards the cache and replaces the mutex with per-shard atomics/lock-free list. ETA today.
kai: Proposed immediate mitigation: merge rollback to restore baseline, then land a targeted fix for cache concurrency. We should also add a microbenchmark that exercises scoring_cache under high concurrency.
jonah: Agreed. rachel, please merge the rollback once CI passes. Then run a canary with the dedupe and lower load first.
rachel: Will do. Also opened an issue tracking KV-cache eviction side effects — noticed eviction jitter increased after the original change which may amplify misses. Issue #789.
maria: Thanks all. I'll attach the repro artifacts and flamegraphs to the bisect ticket.
derek: pushing draft fix PR #4565 now (replace global mutex with sharded cache).
jonah: Plan summary: 1) merge rollback #4561, 2) run small canary, 3) land fix #4565 with microbenchmark and tests, 4) re-run canary. Ops please pause any scheduled capacity changes until canary green.
kai: +1 :thumbsup:
maria: Great catch everyone — this was subtle. Leaving notes in the perf-regressions tracker.
